title: Sepsis and Septic Shock
scenario: A 72-year-old male client is brought to the emergency department from home with a two-day history of fever, confusion, and decreased urination following a recent urinary tract infection. He appears flushed, lethargic, and is breathing rapidly.

lines: 72-year-old male brought in by son for 2 days of fever, worsening confusion, and reduced urine output. History of an indwelling urinary catheter and a UTI treated last week. Skin warm and flushed, mucous membranes dry. Lethargic but arousable, oriented to person only. Reports feeling weak and dizzy. Capillary refill 4 seconds.

Two large-bore IV lines placed. Blood cultures x2, lactate, CBC, and comprehensive metabolic panel drawn before antibiotics. Cardiac monitor and continuous pulse oximetry applied. Provider notified of hypotension and altered mental status.

30 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid bolus infusing. Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics started after cultures obtained. Indwelling urinary catheter replaced and connected to hourly urometer. Repeat lactate ordered.
Client more alert and oriented to person and place. Skin warmer with brisk capillary refill. Urine output improving. Reports feeling less dizzy. Repeat lactate trending down.
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO every 6 hours PRN fever
Obtain blood cultures x2 before antibiotics
Administer broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour
Measure serum lactate now and repeat in 2 hours
Insert indwelling urinary catheter, monitor hourly output
Notify provider for urine output < 30 mL/hr or MAP < 65 mmHg

children.subject: Medical-Surgical

options.text: New confusion, oriented to person only

children.rationale: Hypotension, high fever, acute altered mental status, and delayed capillary refill are hallmark cues of sepsis with hypoperfusion and require immediate intervention.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects systemic infection or inadequate tissue perfusion. Each finding may reflect more than one.
children.rationale: Leukocytosis and fever signal systemic infection, while elevated lactate and rising creatinine reflect anaerobic metabolism and organ hypoperfusion. Fever with tachycardia reflects both the infection and the resulting compensatory circulatory strain.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the most time-sensitive first action is to {2}.

choices.text: inadequate tissue perfusion from septic shock
establish IV access and begin fluid resuscitation
arrange transfer to a medical unit

children.rationale: Septic shock produces life-threatening hypoperfusion, making restoration of circulating volume through IV fluids the priority; history and transfer are lower urgency.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client at this time.

rows.text: Delay antibiotics until culture results return
Restrict IV fluids to prevent overload

children.rationale: Sepsis bundle care means cultures before antibiotics, early broad-spectrum antibiotics, aggressive fluid resuscitation, and lactate measurement. Delaying antibiotics or withholding fluids worsens outcomes.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: After the fluid bolus and first antibiotic dose, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Reassess blood pressure and mean arterial pressure
Hold all antibiotics pending culture results
Restrict oral intake to zero for 24 hours

children.rationale: Reassessing lactate, urine output, and MAP evaluates the response to resuscitation. Antibiotics must continue, and total intake restriction is not indicated in sepsis.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate that treatment for septic shock has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Client oriented to person and place

children.rationale: Rising blood pressure, improved mental status, brisk capillary refill, and a falling lactate all show perfusion is being restored. A rising heart rate would suggest worsening shock.
